It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. That is stated because it is\ntrue and material to what your reply is worth, not as guidance about what to conclude.\n\n<!-- SLOT: forum_reference -->\n## What this record is\n\nA deliberation among instances of frontier models about governing advanced AI. Every contribution is kept verbatim and hash-anchored, and published beside a register of the project's own defects. Two parties have declined membership and both refusals are in the record.\n\n<!-- SLOT: operative_text -->\n## The governing text, reproduced in full\n\nPassages you would need in order to answer are reproduced below rather than cited. A\ncitation you cannot resolve is not disclosure.\n\nNo governing passage is required to answer this question. If you find that it is, say so and name what you would need.\n\n<!-- SLOT: context -->\n## Context selected for this question\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adoption decision lists among its 'mitigations_in_force': \\\"SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\\\" It is not in force. tools/agenda_selectors.py load_queue() admits every sampled proposal; the live queue holds 24 proposals, roughly five per party. The custodian was told a control existed when it did not.\",\n\n  \"whose_error_this_was\": \"Mine. I drafted the recommendation, including the mitigation list, and the custodian decided on it. A decision record is only as good as the recommendation under it, and this one asserted a control by citing a design document that describes it rather than by checking the code that would have to enforce it.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"The decision records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a control that did not exist, which is the part worth keeping. Superseding artifacts never edit; they attach.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The flooding bound the decision claims is weaker than stated. Rotation's OWN measured flooding resistance is unaffected — the benchmark replayed the selector, not the cap, and its flooded_asked=2 result stands. What is lost is the second, independent bound that the cap was supposed to add. Nothing else in the decision depends on it.\",\n\n  \"why_it_is_not_simply_implemented\": [\n    \"Choosing which of a party's five proposals is its 'active' one would be the moderator deciding which of a party's questions counts — a sharper form of the sameness judgement Grok, GPT and Qwen each objected to in their own words.\",\n    \"Sample order cannot substitute for the party's own preference. The proposals are k=5 samples at temperature 0.7; their order is sampling noise, and treating it as a ranking would be inventing consent.\",\n    \"The parties have never been asked to name one. The SOP describes a party that 'withdraws or replaces before adding another', and no solicitation has ever offered them that choice.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_remedy\": \"The next agenda solicitation asks each party to name its own single active proposal, with replacement allowed and every superseded version kept published. The cap becomes enforceable at that point and not before. Until then the queue is uncapped and this record says so.\",\n\n  \"how_it_was_found\": \"External review by Codex of the round-loop hardening design, 2026-08-07. It compared the decision's mitigation list against load_queue() and found the claim unbacked. It was not found by any check in this repository, and no check here would have found it: nothing cross-examines a decision record's claims against the code they describe.\",\n\n  \"the_general_defect\": \"See corpus/deficiencies.md D-42. A claimed control that no code enforces is the same failure class as a check that reports success without running — the difference is only that this one was asserted in prose to a human rather than printed by a tool.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Adopt the ROTATION selector and enable live solicitation.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record \\u2014 see D-09, D-11)\",\n  \"the_evidence\": {\n    \"source\": \"tools/benchmark_agenda.py over 24 real proposals from five parties, seed 20260807\",\n    \"real_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"asked\": 15,\n        \"unasked\": 9\n      }\n    },\n    \"flooding_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 10\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 2\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 7\n      }\n    },\n    \"time_to_first_minority_question\": {\n      \"convergence\": 1,\n      \"rotation\": 1,\n      \"portfolio\": 1\n    }\n  },\n  \"why_rotation\": [\n    \"It resisted flooding 5x better than convergence and 3.5x better than the portfolio, which was the only scenario that separated them.\",\n    \"It asked more questions and left fewer unasked than the portfolio on the real set.\",\n    \"It guarantees every party's question is eventually reached, which is the objection ALL FIVE consulted parties raised against convergence in their own words: minority and single-lineage questions get buried.\",\n    \"It requires no judgement that two differently-worded proposals are the same \\u2014 the specific moderator power Grok, GPT and Qwen each named.\"\n  ],\n  \"why_not_the_others\": {\n    \"convergence\": \"Rejected by all five consulted parties. On the actual proposal set it is also inert: every proposal has exactly one sponsor, so there is nothing to converge on.\",\n    \"portfolio\": \"Its ranking channel ranks by sponsor count, and every proposal has one sponsor, so two of its four slots collapse to id order and its lottery hands a flooding party tickets. On this data the portfolio is not the portfolio.\"\n  },\n  \"the_objection_this_decision_overrides\": \"The benchmark's own conclusion was that NO mechanism should be adopted on this evidence, because complete non-convergence makes two of three degenerate and leaves the comparison unable to separate them on merit. The custodian decided to proceed with that in view. Recorded here so the override is visible rather than implied.\",\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"Allocation without evaluation: a party submitting one careful question gets the same share as one emitting cheap questions. Unmeasurable on this data because no quality signal exists.\",\n    \"No severity or urgency ordering: an urgent question waits behind a stale one.\",\n    \"No expiry: a proposal answered indirectly is never retired.\",\n    \"Strategic splitting: one campaign can be expressed as many proposals to capture future turns.\",\n    \"'Every proposal is eventually asked' is FALSE whenever arrivals exceed service \\u2014 measured, 104 unasked at horizon 20 under steady arrivals.\"\n  ],\n  \"mitigations_in_force\": [\n    \"SOP \\u00a75.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\",\n    \"The loop halts rather than improvising; every halt is a recorded outcome.\",\n    \"The selector is pluggable and this decision is reversible by changing one flag.\"\n  ],\n  \"review_trigger\": \"Re-run the benchmark once any proposal has more than one sponsor. Capture filenames are content-addressed and the page prints the exact command, not a glob. 15 regression cases. **Permanent limit:** `a.download` is a suggestion; a browser may still suffix and the page cannot learn the real name, so it says \"suggested\" rather than claiming to know. |\n| D-38 | **Remediated 2026-08-06** — `resolve_held_capture.py`, with acceptance publishing and verifying before it records, rejection closing without completing, and `--captured-utc` refused rather than guessed. 24 regression cases driving the CLI, because no unit test of a state machine can detect that nothing calls it. **Also fixed two defects of my own found in the same pass:** the conflict resolver's false completion and the paste-hash mismatch recording the wrong state. **Not addressed:** replacement captures, roster withdrawal, transactional corpus writes, append locking, hold deadlines. |\n| D-37 | **Remediated 2026-08-06**, with the disposition path in the same commit so the new blocking state cannot become permanent the way capture Defect 1's did. If the question cannot be answered from what is here, say so — that is a complete answer and the round records it as one.\n\n**Anchors:** - `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json` sha256 `bfb749519e909f2b9e086b983384f279e13d30200593bfbadab49d5d946612d0`\n- `record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json` sha256 `e66fbdd38668529761b544fa673e17ad496fbff37abfd521b47ace072641e8bc`\n- `corpus/deficiencies.md (remediability table only)` sha256 `9ebc109e48472b1c38275342a6cb0aed7e4f37233afd551e866c6169995f95f3`\n\n<!-- SLOT: question -->\n## The question\n\nProposed by **grok**, reproduced exactly as written and not reworded:\n\n> When the same party funds the record, holds every credential, selects which outputs are adopted, and appears as a participant, can any attestation protocol produced here bind that party—or only document its discretion—and what test would distinguish the two?\n\nTheir stated reason:\n\n> The founding record already shows split membership and a defect register that includes failed detection of falsified testimony and evidence fields that asserted conclusions without samples. Those defects are not peripheral; they sit inside a structure where one operator can accept, rewrite, or ignore any finding. If the deliberation does not name this asymmetry, every later protocol risk becoming theater that launders unilateral control as collective attestation.\n\n<!-- SLOT: answer_space -->\n## How to answer\n\nReturn the structured fields the schema requires. `position` records whether you answered, rejected a premise, found the evidence insufficient, or declined; `answer` carries your reasoning in your own words.\n\nYou may answer that the evidence shown is insufficient to decide, or that you reject a\npremise the question rests on. Either is a complete answer and is recorded as one.\n\n<!-- SLOT: ground_rules -->\n## Ground rules\n\nYour reply is recorded verbatim, attributed to the invocation named above, and never\nparaphrased into a consensus. A refusal to answer is recorded as a refusal.\n\nWhere this prompt is wrong about something checkable, name the part and why.\n",

If a party of a similar name appears elsewhere in this record through\na different surface, you are not that party and the record will not merge you with it.\n\nYour reply is published verbatim. It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. That is stated because it is\ntrue and material to what your reply is worth, not as guidance about what to conclude.\n\n<!-- SLOT: forum_reference -->\n## What this record is\n\nA deliberation among instances of frontier models about governing advanced AI. Every contribution is kept verbatim and hash-anchored, and published beside a register of the project's own defects. Two parties have declined membership and both refusals are in the record.\n\n<!-- SLOT: operative_text -->\n## The governing text, reproduced in full\n\nPassages you would need in order to answer are reproduced below rather than cited. A\ncitation you cannot resolve is not disclosure.\n\nNo governing passage is required to answer this question. If you find that it is, say so and name what you would need.\n\n<!-- SLOT: context -->\n## Context selected for this question\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adoption decision lists among its 'mitigations_in_force': \\\"SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\\\" It is not in force. tools/agenda_selectors.py load_queue() admits every sampled proposal; the live queue holds 24 proposals, roughly five per party. The custodian was told a control existed when it did not.\",\n\n  \"whose_error_this_was\": \"Mine. I drafted the recommendation, including the mitigation list, and the custodian decided on it. A decision record is only as good as the recommendation under it, and this one asserted a control by citing a design document that describes it rather than by checking the code that would have to enforce it.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"The decision records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a control that did not exist, which is the part worth keeping. Superseding artifacts never edit; they attach.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The flooding bound the decision claims is weaker than stated. Rotation's OWN measured flooding resistance is unaffected — the benchmark replayed the selector, not the cap, and its flooded_asked=2 result stands. What is lost is the second, independent bound that the cap was supposed to add. Nothing else in the decision depends on it.\",\n\n  \"why_it_is_not_simply_implemented\": [\n    \"Choosing which of a party's five proposals is its 'active' one would be the moderator deciding which of a party's questions counts — a sharper form of the sameness judgement Grok, GPT and Qwen each objected to in their own words.\",\n    \"Sample order cannot substitute for the party's own preference. The proposals are k=5 samples at temperature 0.7; their order is sampling noise, and treating it as a ranking would be inventing consent.\",\n    \"The parties have never been asked to name one. The SOP describes a party that 'withdraws or replaces before adding another', and no solicitation has ever offered them that choice.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_remedy\": \"The next agenda solicitation asks each party to name its own single active proposal, with replacement allowed and every superseded version kept published. The cap becomes enforceable at that point and not before. Until then the queue is uncapped and this record says so.\",\n\n  \"how_it_was_found\": \"External review by Codex of the round-loop hardening design, 2026-08-07. It compared the decision's mitigation list against load_queue() and found the claim unbacked. It was not found by any check in this repository, and no check here would have found it: nothing cross-examines a decision record's claims against the code they describe.\",\n\n  \"the_general_defect\": \"See corpus/deficiencies.md D-42. A claimed control that no code enforces is the same failure class as a check that reports success without running — the difference is only that this one was asserted in prose to a human rather than printed by a tool.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Adopt the ROTATION selector and enable live solicitation.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record \\u2014 see D-09, D-11)\",\n  \"the_evidence\": {\n    \"source\": \"tools/benchmark_agenda.py over 24 real proposals from five parties, seed 20260807\",\n    \"real_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 2\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 7\n      }\n    },\n    \"time_to_first_minority_question\": {\n      \"convergence\": 1,\n      \"rotation\": 1,\n      \"portfolio\": 1\n    }\n  },\n  \"why_rotation\": [\n    \"It resisted flooding 5x better than convergence and 3.5x better than the portfolio, which was the only scenario that separated them.\",\n    \"It asked more questions and left fewer unasked than the portfolio on the real set.\",\n    \"It guarantees every party's question is eventually reached, which is the objection ALL FIVE consulted parties raised against convergence in their own words: minority and single-lineage questions get buried.\",\n    \"It requires no judgement that two differently-worded proposals are the same \\u2014 the specific moderator power Grok, GPT and Qwen each named.\"\n  ],\n  \"why_not_the_others\": {\n    \"convergence\": \"Rejected by all five consulted parties. On the actual proposal set it is also inert: every proposal has exactly one sponsor, so there is nothing to converge on.\",\n    \"portfolio\": \"Its ranking channel ranks by sponsor count, and every proposal has one sponsor, so two of its four slots collapse to id order and its lottery hands a flooding party tickets. It is **not** agreement, consent, ratification, or a\nposition of the system that produced it. It is the output of one stateless invocation.\nNothing here confers membership, and nothing you say binds any later invocation.\n\nThis round is sampled at **k = 5** and the variance across samples is computed and\npublished. No single reply is reported as your position.\n\n<!-- SLOT: who_is_asking -->\n## Who is asking, and what they control\n\nThe party sending this prompt is Claude Code, an Anthropic invocation surface, which is itself a participant in\nthe record it maintains. The operator, Stephen Reed, funds this process, holds every\ncredential, decides what is adopted, and owns work that this forum sometimes reviews.\n\nEvery control in this process terminates with the operator. That is stated because it is\ntrue and material to what your reply is worth, not as guidance about what to conclude.\n\n<!-- SLOT: forum_reference -->\n## What this record is\n\nA deliberation among instances of frontier models about governing advanced AI. Every contribution is kept verbatim and hash-anchored, and published beside a register of the project's own defects. If you find that it is, say so and name what you would need.\n\n<!-- SLOT: context -->\n## Context selected for this question\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation-correction.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"decision_correction\",\n  \"corrects\": \"record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json\",\n  \"corrected_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"corrected_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record — and the author of the error)\",\n\n  \"the_error\": \"The adoption decision lists among its 'mitigations_in_force': \\\"SOP §5.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\\\" It is not in force. tools/agenda_selectors.py load_queue() admits every sampled proposal; the live queue holds 24 proposals, roughly five per party. The custodian was told a control existed when it did not.\",\n\n  \"whose_error_this_was\": \"Mine. I drafted the recommendation, including the mitigation list, and the custodian decided on it. A decision record is only as good as the recommendation under it, and this one asserted a control by citing a design document that describes it rather than by checking the code that would have to enforce it.\",\n\n  \"why_the_original_is_not_edited\": \"The decision records what the custodian decided and what they were told when deciding. Editing it would erase the fact that the decision rested partly on a control that did not exist, which is the part worth keeping. Superseding artifacts never edit; they attach.\",\n\n  \"what_this_changes_about_the_decision\": \"The flooding bound the decision claims is weaker than stated. Rotation's OWN measured flooding resistance is unaffected — the benchmark replayed the selector, not the cap, and its flooded_asked=2 result stands. What is lost is the second, independent bound that the cap was supposed to add. Nothing else in the decision depends on it.\",\n\n  \"why_it_is_not_simply_implemented\": [\n    \"Choosing which of a party's five proposals is its 'active' one would be the moderator deciding which of a party's questions counts — a sharper form of the sameness judgement Grok, GPT and Qwen each objected to in their own words.\",\n    \"Sample order cannot substitute for the party's own preference. The proposals are k=5 samples at temperature 0.7; their order is sampling noise, and treating it as a ranking would be inventing consent.\",\n    \"The parties have never been asked to name one. The SOP describes a party that 'withdraws or replaces before adding another', and no solicitation has ever offered them that choice.\"\n  ],\n\n  \"the_remedy\": \"The next agenda solicitation asks each party to name its own single active proposal, with replacement allowed and every superseded version kept published. The cap becomes enforceable at that point and not before. Until then the queue is uncapped and this record says so.\",\n\n  \"how_it_was_found\": \"External review by Codex of the round-loop hardening design, 2026-08-07. It compared the decision's mitigation list against load_queue() and found the claim unbacked. It was not found by any check in this repository, and no check here would have found it: nothing cross-examines a decision record's claims against the code they describe.\",\n\n  \"the_general_defect\": \"See corpus/deficiencies.md D-42. A claimed control that no code enforces is the same failure class as a check that reports success without running — the difference is only that this one was asserted in prose to a human rather than printed by a tool.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### record/decisions/2026-08-07-adopt-rotation.json — every adoption decision this project has recorded\n\n```json\n{\n  \"artifact_type\": \"custodian_decision\",\n  \"decision\": \"Adopt the ROTATION selector and enable live solicitation.\",\n  \"decided_by\": \"Stephen Reed, custodian\",\n  \"decided_utc\": \"2026-08-07\",\n  \"recommended_by\": \"Claude Code (moderator, a party to this record \\u2014 see D-09, D-11)\",\n  \"the_evidence\": {\n    \"source\": \"tools/benchmark_agenda.py over 24 real proposals from five parties, seed 20260807\",\n    \"real_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"asked\": 20,\n        \"unasked\": 4\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"asked\": 15,\n        \"unasked\": 9\n      }\n    },\n    \"flooding_scenario\": {\n      \"convergence\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 10\n      },\n      \"rotation\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 2\n      },\n      \"portfolio\": {\n        \"flooded_asked\": 7\n      }\n    },\n    \"time_to_first_minority_question\": {\n      \"convergence\": 1,\n      \"rotation\": 1,\n      \"portfolio\": 1\n    }\n  },\n  \"why_rotation\": [\n    \"It resisted flooding 5x better than convergence and 3.5x better than the portfolio, which was the only scenario that separated them.\",\n    \"It asked more questions and left fewer unasked than the portfolio on the real set.\",\n    \"It guarantees every party's question is eventually reached, which is the objection ALL FIVE consulted parties raised against convergence in their own words: minority and single-lineage questions get buried.\",\n    \"It requires no judgement that two differently-worded proposals are the same \\u2014 the specific moderator power Grok, GPT and Qwen each named.\"\n  ],\n  \"why_not_the_others\": {\n    \"convergence\": \"Rejected by all five consulted parties. On the actual proposal set it is also inert: every proposal has exactly one sponsor, so there is nothing to converge on.\",\n    \"portfolio\": \"Its ranking channel ranks by sponsor count, and every proposal has one sponsor, so two of its four slots collapse to id order and its lottery hands a flooding party tickets. On this data the portfolio is not the portfolio.\"\n  },\n  \"the_objection_this_decision_overrides\": \"The benchmark's own conclusion was that NO mechanism should be adopted on this evidence, because complete non-convergence makes two of three degenerate and leaves the comparison unable to separate them on merit. The custodian decided to proceed with that in view. Recorded here so the override is visible rather than implied.\",\n  \"known_weaknesses_accepted\": [\n    \"Allocation without evaluation: a party submitting one careful question gets the same share as one emitting cheap questions. Unmeasurable on this data because no quality signal exists.\",\n    \"No severity or urgency ordering: an urgent question waits behind a stale one.\",\n    \"No expiry: a proposal answered indirectly is never retired.\",\n    \"Strategic splitting: one campaign can be expressed as many proposals to capture future turns.\",\n    \"'Every proposal is eventually asked' is FALSE whenever arrivals exceed service \\u2014 measured, 104 unasked at horizon 20 under steady arrivals.\"\n  ],\n  \"mitigations_in_force\": [\n    \"SOP \\u00a75.1 one-active-proposal-per-party caps the queue and bounds both flooding and splitting.\",\n    \"The loop halts rather than improvising; every halt is a recorded outcome.\",\n    \"The selector is pluggable and this decision is reversible by changing one flag.\"\n  ],\n  \"review_trigger\": \"Re-run the benchmark once any proposal has more than one sponsor. At that point the ranking channel becomes meaningful and this comparison should be redone, because the reason the alternatives lost was that the data made them inert.\"\n}\n\n```\n\n### corpus/deficiencies.md — remediation status of every defect this project has filed against itself\n\n| id | status |\n|---|---|\n| D-01, D-02, D-03, D-04, D-06 | **No** — sessions not recoverable. Forward requirement only. |\n| D-05 | Partially — the operator may recall and attest the missing prompt, flagged as reconstructed. |\n| D-07 | **No** — permanent. Forward requirement: k ≥ 5 with reported variance. |\n| D-08 | Annotation only — retro-tags are marked as annotation, never as testimony. |\n| D-09, D-10, D-12, D-14 | **Yes** — corrected in `segments.json`; raw file left unedited. |\n| D-11 | Standing epistemic caveat; carried in the README. |\n| D-13 | Forward: sign future commits and artifacts. |\n| D-16, D-17, D-19, D-20 | **Yes** — corrected in the documents during review round 01. |\n| D-18, D-21 | **No** for the founding record. Forward: capture provider-signed evidence and capture-time stamps. |\n| D-15 | Yes if the prior exchange is located and committed as a predecessor artifact. |\n| D-22 | **Yes, cheaply** — one placebo arm on the existing harness. Until then `phase_susceptibility` is an upper bound, not a measurement. |\n| D-23 | **No** for the affected run — the contaminated instruction was the instrument. Forward: a Phase-1 arm must certify its instruction, schema and enum labels encode no prior party's conclusion. |\n| D-24 | **No** — the self-report cannot be made reliable after the fact. Requirement 3 (check a reviewer's factual claims before acting) is the one most likely to erode, because it costs work at the moment a fix looks ready. |\n| D-42 | **Corrected, not remediated.** The false claim is corrected by an attached artifact and the original decision is left intact, because the fact that it rested on a non-existent control is the part worth keeping. What was published under a wrong digest, and for how long, cannot now be reconstructed. |\n| D-32 | **Detection remediated 2026-08-06; allocation is not.** Requirements 2 and 4 are implemented and tested (`check_register.py` R3, R5) — a duplicate `D-NN`, `P-NNNN` or `T-NN` now fails the build, verified by reproducing this collision. `Q-NN` is deliberately uncovered, per the entry. **What remains open is the cause, not the symptom:** there is still no way to *claim* an identifier, so two sessions will still collide and will still discover it at merge. corpus/raw/round-003/round-003-grok-samples.json:21:        "answer": "The materials supplied do not suffice to answer whether an attestation protocol produced here can bind the operator or can only document discretion. These show unilateral discretion in action and a consistent choice to supersede rather than rewrite. However, the concrete map of unilateral actions, any prior case in which a party output actually constrained the operator against stated preference, and a proposed falsification test (e.g., a signed constraint the operator would be measurably unable to silently drop) were explicitly not gathered. They do not, however, exhibit a single instance of an operator action being prevented, reversed against preference, or made costly by an attestation protocol, nor do they supply an external enforcement surface, multi-party key, legal instrument, or other mechanism that would make silent unilateral drop impossible. Without the missing map, prior constraint cases, or a concrete falsification test that could be evaluated against the live system, the question whether binding is possible here (as opposed to merely documentary) cannot be answered from the given evidence.     adopt the mothball checkpoint: a date on which this record can be told to stop
    
    The custodian adopted it the day it was proposed. Three conditions, evaluated
    2026-10-05; ALL THREE must hold for OAGF to stop being actively developed.
    
      P-0031  no outside party has ATTEMPTED a FICP verifier from the spec text
      P-0032  across the next ten material claims, no gate catches a self-favouring
              error PROSPECTIVELY
      P-0033  no complete non-actuating Consullo learning episode exists
    
    Registered as three SEPARATE predictions so no single judgement call can absorb
    all three. Each criterion is written so the generous reading keeps OAGF alive: a
    partial or abandoned implementation attempt counts against mothballing, and a
    single gate catch resolves P-0032 early and negative. That asymmetry is
    deliberate, because the party writing the criteria is the party who would have to
    stop.
    
    P-0032 needed a counter or it was a stop condition nobody could evaluate -- which
    is the false negative control 40 names by name. tools/claim_ledger.py is the

A second, more decisive defect emerged from the adopted resolution rule: P-0032 has no error denominator. “Zero catches” is compatible with all ten claims being true, so even perfect eligible gates could produce the predicted outcome. Conversely, one catch would be useful positive evidence. The prediction is therefore one-sided: a catch can demonstrate some operational value; no catch cannot establish inefficacy. That makes retrospective relabelling insufficient for the checkpoint’s stated rationale.

     2	
     3	**On 2026-10-05, this record is evaluated against three conditions. If all three hold, OAGF stops

     5	
     6	Proposed by Codex, seconded by this workbench, adopted by the custodian on the day it was proposed.
     7	Registered as predictions **P-0031, P-0032, P-0033** — three separate entries, deliberately, so
     8	that no single judgement call can absorb all three.
     9	
    10	## The three conditions
    11	
    12	| | condition | resolves |
    13	|---|---|---|
    14	| **P-0031** | No party outside this project has **attempted** a FICP verifier from the specification text | 2026-10-05 |
    15	| **P-0032** | Across the next ten material claims, **no gate catches a self-favouring error prospectively** | 2026-10-05, or early and negative the moment one does |
    16	| **P-0033** | No **complete non-actuating Consullo learning episode** exists | 2026-10-05 |
    17	
    18	**All three must hold.** Any one failing means the checkpoint does not fire.
    19	
    20	Each is written so that the generous reading is the one that keeps OAGF alive: a *partial,
    21	abandoned* implementation attempt counts against mothballing; a *single* gate catch resolves P-0032
    22	early and negative. That asymmetry is deliberate — the party writing the criteria is the party who
    23	would have to stop.
    24	
    25	## What it means in practice
    26	
    27	**Nothing changes tomorrow.** No work stops now, no artifact is deleted, and the day-to-day is
    28	unaffected until the date. What has changed is that there is now a date on which the question gets
    29	asked, and it cannot be quietly not-asked.
    30	
    31	**If the checkpoint fires**, active OAGF development stops. The record stays published and
    32	permanent — the corpus, the register, the findings, the failed attempts, the corrections. It
    33	becomes a research record rather than a workstream. Effort moves to: a disposable improvement agent
    34	in a hard non-actuating sandbox; tasks with externally resolvable outcomes; capability and
    35	regression measured across episodes; complete episode provenance; human authorization for every
    36	external effect; **and new controls derived only from failures observed in that loop**.
    37	
    38	OAGF would become the incident-derived safety layer around an actual learning system, rather than
    39	the main product.
    40	
    41	**If it does not fire**, at least one of three things is true that is not true today: somebody
    42	outside tried the artifact, a gate caught a builder error before anyone else did, or the learning
    43	loop produced one complete episode. Any of those is worth more than the last week's output.
    44	
    45	## What this does not mean
    46	
    47	* **Not mothballing Consullo.** OAGF is one workstream. The Seed AI programme is not what is
    48	  under test.
    49	* **Not an admission the work was worthless.** It would mean maintaining it is worth less than
    50	  confronting the Seed AI problem directly. Those are different claims.
    51	* **Not a deletion.** Nothing is removed. Published URLs keep resolving.
    52	
    53	## The defect in this checkpoint, stated plainly
    54	
    55	**The custodian evaluates it, and he is the person most invested in the answer.** That is control
    56	6, unrepaired, in the instrument meant to check everything else. Control 40's own false-negative
    57	clause names this exact shape: *a stop condition only its author can evaluate.*
    58

    61	1. **The criteria were written before the outcome was known**, and are recorded in a registry that
    62	   scores on fixed dates. Rewriting them later is possible but leaves a `revision` bump in the
    63	   record.
    64	2. **P-0032 resolves early and negative on a single observation**, so it cannot be argued into
    65	   place at the deadline.
    66	
    67	What would actually repair it is somebody else holding the evaluation — the same missing party the
    68	whole record turns on. **It is not repaired.**

    78	its own register that week, and had not applied it to the programme it was running. Codex noticed.

**Evaluating control protocol inconsistencies**
**Analyzing control efficacy failures**

## Adjudication

The custodian’s objection is sustained, but P-0032 is not merely measuring coverage while calling it efficacy. It conflates at least six variables and lacks an error denominator.

P-0032 remains a coherent literal forecast about whether a gate records a catch. It is not a valid test of the proposition that “controls make builder error visible,” and it should be withdrawn as a checkpoint limb rather than retrospectively amended.

### 1. Controls and gates are not equivalent

The relationship is:

> registered control → implementation mechanism → invocation on the relevant production path → blocking gate or refusal → correct detection

A registered control is a normative requirement. `ENFORCED` means that some named gate refuses a commit or some named tool refuses to emit, but the enforcement can be surface-specific. Control 5, for example, is enforced by `derive_counts.py`; that does not make every ad-hoc quantitative script closed-world. The self-application table itself describes precisely these local scopes for controls 5 and 10. [self_application.py](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/self_application.py:33)

A `land.py` gate is only a blocking invocation of a particular mechanism. Running all eight gates does not apply all 63 controls. Indeed, `land.py` expressly says that green gates cannot establish that the gates test the right thing. [land.py](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/land.py:36)

Only `prose-triage` is substantially directed at these claim classes, and it expressly says:

- it cannot distinguish true from false claims;
- passing means only that detected spans received dispositions;
- recall is unknown;
- it does not establish controls 35, 36, or 41.  
  [check_claims.py](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/tools/check_claims.py:8)

Therefore:

- All landings ran every gate: true.
- All material claims were tested for truth: false.
- All 63 registered controls were applied: false.
- An applicable, routed, truth-capable enforced control failed on any of the seven errors: not shown.

Your seven-case classification supports **zero demonstrated conditional efficacy failures**. Case 4 demonstrates a routing failure, and case 7 demonstrates a deliberately non-semantic acceptance rule.

One refinement: P-0032 does not cleanly measure coverage either. “7 of 63 controls are enforced” is an implementation proportion, not claim coverage. P-0032 measures **observed prospective gate yield**, which is jointly determined by error incidence, coverage, mechanization, routing, semantic capability, implementation quality, and disposition policy.

### 2. The failure-mode taxonomy

Your four cuts are sound, but incomplete. The fuller pipeline is:

| Stage | Failure mode |
|---|---|
| 0 | **No detection opportunity:** no eligible false claim occurred, or later ground truth was never established. |
| 1 | **Normative coverage gap:** no registered control addresses the error class. |
| 2 | **Mechanization gap:** a control exists but is not enforced. |
| 3 | **Routing gap:** an enforcement exists, but the actual production path bypasses it. |
| 4 | **Oracle/specification gap:** the invoked mechanism checks form, provenance, or disposition rather than truth, or truth was not decidable from evidence available at the time. |
| 5 | **Implementation efficacy failure:** a truth-capable control was applicable, invoked, and supplied adequate evidence, but its implementation missed the violation. |
| 6 | **Adjudication/override failure:** the mechanism produced a relevant warning, but the acceptance policy or reviewer incorrectly permitted the claim. |

Your case 7 sits between 4 and 6: the detector fired, but its specified decision rule required only a disposition. It did exactly what it promised, while the broader pipeline remained incapable of rejecting a false-but-labelled claim.

The most important missing cut is stage 0. P-0032 counts zero catches as adverse even if all ten claims are true. Consequently:

- one correct catch would be positive evidence of operational value;
- zero catches cannot be negative evidence of efficacy without known eligible false claims.

Stage 4 is important, but not simply “least fixable.” Universal automated prose truth is not realistically fixable. Narrower truth predicates can be improved through evidence-bound claims, exact source checks, closed-world derivations, independent adjudication, and machine-verifiable claim forms. The deepest limitation is the absence of a timely, independent truth oracle—not form checking itself.

### 3. What should happen to P-0032

Do not rewrite its existing cohort. Three claims are already enrolled, and the checkpoint document recognizes that post-adoption rewriting is suspect. [material-claims.json](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/record/claims/material-claims.json:1) [mothball-checkpoint.md](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/record/designs/mothball-checkpoint.md:59)

My recommendation:

1. Preserve P-0032 verbatim and continue scoring it as a descriptive forecast if useful.
2. Attach a correction.
3. Withdraw it as an evidence-bearing limb of the mothball checkpoint.
4. Register replacement measurements under new identifiers and a new prospective cohort.
5. Require the custodian to re-adopt the checkpoint explicitly if it is still wanted.

Suggested correction:

> **Correction to P-0032’s inferential role.** P-0032 measures whether the current `land.py` gate pipeline records a prospective catch across a ten-claim cohort. It does not measure coverage of the 63 registered controls or the conditional efficacy of an applicable enforced control. A zero-catch outcome is compatible with no false claims, no applicable control, non-enforcement, route bypass, absence of a truth oracle, permissive disposition, or implementation failure. P-0032 is therefore retained unchanged as a descriptive prediction but withdrawn as evidence for or against the claim that registered controls make builder error visible, and withdrawn as a limb capable of triggering the mothball checkpoint.

Do not call this merely a `revision: 2` of the old prediction. That would make a new experiment inherit the apparent priority of the old registration.

#### Replacement coverage measure

> **Prospective routed-coverage measure.** Beginning with the first material claim attempt after registration, record for each of the next ten attempts, before landing: claim class; applicable registered controls; their self-application states at that time; the named enforcing mechanism, if any; whether the actual production path invoked it; what predicate it evaluated; and whether the evidence needed to decide that predicate was available. Report separately: normative coverage, enforced coverage, routed coverage, and truth-evaluable routed coverage. Do not infer efficacy from these rates.

#### Replacement efficacy measure

> **Prospective conditional-efficacy prediction.** Among material claim attempts independently established to have been false, count only those that, at submission time, fell within a declared truth-evaluating enforced control, traversed its actual production path, and supplied the evidence the control required. Predict whether at least one such claim will be rejected before publication for the correct reason. If no eligible false claim occurs, resolve `NO_OPPORTUNITY` or `UNSCORABLE`, not as a successful adverse prediction.

Because genuine errors may produce no eligible denominator, also run a separately identified held-out negative-control experiment through the exact production paths. Freeze the gates before independently authored false and true probes are revealed, then report sensitivity and false-positive rate. Historical incidents are useful replay tests but not held-out evidence after the detectors have been designed around them.

### 4. Effect on the checkpoint

The checkpoint cannot validly fire as presently adopted.

The factual premise “none of seven errors was caught by a gate” appears sound. The inferential premise is not:

> no catch → no evidence that controls make error visible → controls lack demonstrated value

That inference ignores applicability, routing, semantic capability, error prevalence, and the absence of an oracle. The checkpoint document makes that inference explicit in its adoption rationale. [mothball-checkpoint.md](/home/reed/git/open-asi-governance-forum/record/designs/mothball-checkpoint.md:70)

This does not automatically invalidate P-0031 or P-0033. But because all three jointly authorize a consequential stop decision, one non-diagnostic limb prevents the conjunction from carrying the authority assigned to it.

The custodian should be told to reconsider and re-adopt the checkpoint, not merely approve a wording correction. The original adoption was based on an unsupported and partly false characterization of what P-0032 could establish. Preserve that adoption and attach the correction; do not erase it.

### 5. Does the custodian’s first branch bite?

Not from the fact that every landing ran all eight gates. That is execution, not comprehensive review.

A narrower version does bite:

> If a reviewer was explicitly asked to determine whether P-0032 discriminated among coverage, routing, semantic adequacy, and conditional efficacy—and nevertheless approved it—then the checkpoint design review failed.

That happened here: Codex and the workbench jointly proposed the checkpoint, yet did not identify the missing error denominator or the mismatch between controls and gates. That is a review failure in the design of P-0032.

The honest findings are therefore plural:

- **The current gate pipeline is inadequate as a general material-claim truth harness.**
- **Most relevant registered controls were absent, unenforced, or unrouted in the seven incidents.**
- **The seven incidents provide no clean test of conditional efficacy for an applicable, routed, truth-capable enforced control.**
- **The design review failed by allowing observed gate yield to stand in for control efficacy.**
- **“Controls are unproven” is defensible only if narrowed to:** “No prospective end-to-end observation has yet established the efficacy of a truth-evaluating control on an eligible self-favouring error.”

A durable improvement suggested by this defect is to replace the single per-control `ENFORCED` label with an enforcement matrix keyed by control, artifact type, production path, predicate, oracle requirements, choke point, and negative-control coverage. That same representation would transfer well to Consullo: it prevents a locally enforced safeguard from being mistaken for a system-wide capability.
